science.title: Near-total lunar eclipse to be visible from Saskatchewan in August
science.description: Saskatchewan residents will have an opportunity to watch a near-total lunar eclipse later this month, with the moon expected to take on a reddish appearance as it passes through Earth's shadow. The partial lunar eclipse will occur overnight from Aug. 27 into Aug. 28, according to information shared by Abigail Sadowski, a resident Astra member with the Calum Observatory in Regina. Approximately 96 per cent of the moon is expected to pass through Earth's dark umbral shadow, bringing the event close to totality. Sadowski said the moon will change in appearance as it moves through the shadow. “You'll start to see the moon turning kind of red, and then it looks like it gets kind of to its maximum around 10:19 p.m.,” Sadowski said.
